checked_scope: All source project optimizer/profit, sharp scalar gain bounds and effort-only inversion; all review profit-box attainability, transformed joint linear feasibility set/support certificate, richer profit-effort identification and degeneracy cases.
checks_performed: Read exact pinned source and contribution metadata; actual manuscript SHA256 agrees with provenance and review metadata.

Differentiated the strictly concave project objective and checked B=0, a=0, branch continuity and monotonicity; independently derived beta(1-beta) consumption-equivalent exponent from date-one utility and all-date baseline scaling.
Verified continuous lower-to-upper primitive interpolation hits every firm-profit value and independent primitive boxes allow every joint vector in the Cartesian product of profit intervals.

Rearranged the gain transformation and its inverse to prove necessity and sufficiency of the finite linear system; checked ownership-image support by choosing each profit endpoint according to coefficient sign, including zero coefficients and degenerate intervals.
Checked one-firm cross-household identity and its incompatibility with opposite nondegenerate marginal endpoints.

Derived a=(profit+k z^2/2)/z for z>0 from resource accounting; verified a>kz requires exact binding cap, a=kz permits any weakly larger cap, a<kz contradicts optimality, and z=0 retains the zero-cap obstruction.
limitations: External bibliography and empirical/background attribution were not independently reverified in this audit; approval covers the exact supplied manuscript and the mathematical scope described.
No formal proof-assistant verification or independent human verification; numerical spot checks, where present, supplement analytic checking rather than establish general results.
No claim that the catalogue open problem is solved or that the refinement has priority over external literature.
significance: An implicit joint image is made exactly testable by a transformed linear feasibility system and sharp support certificates; observing profits as well as positive effort identifies returns and often the binding spending limit.
